basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 1.' and it opens '(Cap. XL.—Vers. 1.) Post verba haec, peccavit princeps vinariorum regis Aegypti. Ubi nos'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XL.—Vers. 1.) Post verba haec, peccavit princeps vinariorum regis Aegypti. Ubi nos posuimus, principem vinariorum, in Hebraeo scriptum habet MASEC (משק), illud verbum quod in nomine servi Abraham dudum legimus, quem nos possumus more vulgi vocare pincernam. Nec vile putetur officium, cum apud reges barbaros usque hodie maximae dignitatis sit, regi poculum porrexisse: Poetae quoque de Catamitho et Jove scriptitent, quod amasium suum huic officio manciparit.
